items.title: China's central bank promises policy support, stronger countercyclical adjustments
items.text: The PBOC is shifting its primary short-term operational target from the seven-day repo rate (DR007) to the overnight rate (DR001), with overnight transactions now comprising over 90% of money market repo trading. Despite global tightening trends, the PBOC plans to introduce incremental policy measures to maintain ample liquidity and low financing costs, signaling a divergence from the hawkish stances of the Fed, ECB, and BOJ.

items.title: Imported Inflation Hits as PBOC Flags Overseas Rate Hikes: This Cycle's Impact Seen as Relatively Mild
items.text: The PBOC identifies Middle East geopolitical tensions and the AI-driven demand boom in semiconductors and power as primary drivers of current global supply-side inflationary pressures. While acknowledging global rate hikes, the PBOC expects this cycle of monetary adjustment to be relatively mild, projecting smaller shocks to global financial markets compared to previous tightening episodes.

items.title: UAE central bank’s seat at the dollar table
items.text: The UAE's monetary policy remains structurally tethered to the US dollar, necessitating close alignment with Federal Reserve interest rate decisions to maintain currency stability. This peg forces the UAE central bank to import US monetary conditions, limiting domestic policy autonomy during periods of global economic divergence or localized inflationary shocks.

items.title: We're encouraged by Wednesday's benign inflation data and strong neocloud earnings
items.text: The July CPI report showed benign inflation, reducing market-implied odds of a September Federal Reserve rate hike to 40% and supporting a rally in equities via lower bond yields. Infrastructure-focused cloud providers Coreweave and Nebius saw shares surge 19% and 27% respectively, signaling that massive demand for AI-driven cloud computing remains a primary driver for market performance.

items.title: Small investors became a major stock market force. Now, they risk getting pushed back into the dark
items.text: The SEC is considering a proposal to shift public companies from quarterly to biannual earnings reporting, a move that could create an information vacuum and disadvantage retail investors who rely on frequent disclosures. Market experts warn that reduced transparency could lead to increased misinformation and cause retail participants to become more hesitant toward investing in high-growth, small-cap companies.

items.title: SK Hynix halts bond buying, shifts cash to bank deposits in blow to S.Korean credit market - KED Global
items.text: SK Hynix has abruptly ceased its bond-buying activities, opting instead to move significant cash reserves into commercial bank deposits to prioritize liquidity and potential shareholder returns. This shift by a major corporate issuer creates immediate volatility in the South Korean short-term credit market, potentially forcing other firms to reassess their own liquidity and debt management strategies.

items.title: The $30 trillion Treasury market is facing a painful reckoning. How rising yields could squeeze your portfolio. - MarketWatch
items.text: The $30 trillion U.S. Treasury market is experiencing structural pressure as rising yields threaten to erode the value of existing fixed-income portfolios across the financial sector. Investors must prepare for potential capital losses and increased volatility as the current interest rate environment forces a painful repricing of risk-free assets within institutional and retail portfolios.

items.title: PBOC Q2 Monetary Policy Report: H1 GDP Grows 4.7%, Yuan Strengthens 3% vs Dollar, Creates 1 Trillion Yuan Private Enterprise Relending Facility
items.text: The PBOC has launched a 1 trillion yuan ($149 billion) relending facility specifically for private enterprises, signaling a targeted effort to bolster the private sector amid broader economic structural shifts. Monetary policy is becoming more precise, evidenced by the narrowing of the repo operation corridor to 50 basis points and a 0.25 percentage point rate cut on structural policy tools to lower corporate financing costs.

items.title: Excess savings are driving the new ‘China shock’
items.text: The current 'China shock' is fundamentally different from the past, driven by domestic technological upgrading rather than low-cost labor mobilization, which is creating significant global manufacturing capacity shifts. Weak domestic demand is forcing Chinese firms to export excess production, potentially leading to increased trade tensions as global markets absorb the surge in Chinese manufactured goods.

items.title: Hong Kong property recovery faces new risk as Beijing widens offshore tax net
items.text: Beijing's implementation of a 20% personal income tax on offshore investment returns threatens to dampen mainland demand for Hong Kong real estate and insurance products. UBS analysts estimate this tax could compress net rental yields on residential properties from 2.2% to 1.8%, potentially eroding the asset class's attractiveness to mainland investors.

items.title: HK wins back foreign professionals as financial sector rebounds
items.text: Recruitment data indicates a reversal of the pandemic-era talent drain to Singapore, with seven out of ten fund companies now prioritizing Hong Kong for their Asian base. The resurgence in IPO fundraising and strong performance of the Hang Seng Index are driving renewed demand for office space and professional services, signaling a stabilization in the financial sector.

items.title: Forget chatbot training. AI's next big data grab is about learning how humans work.
items.text: Tech giants are shifting development strategies from static text-based training to 'reinforcement learning environments,' where AI agents simulate real-world workplace tasks like coding and software navigation to improve autonomous performance. Major firms are aggressively securing proprietary behavioral data, with Google reportedly in talks to invest $1.5 billion in startup Mechanize, while Meta and SpaceX are actively collecting internal employee activity data to train next-generation agents.

items.title: From Apple to Netflix: Why Big Tech is pushing deeper into gaming ecosystem
items.text: Big Tech companies are integrating gaming deeper into their hardware and service stacks to increase consumer 'stickiness' and justify high-end silicon upgrades, such as Apple's implementation of hardware-accelerated ray tracing. The strategy focuses on cross-platform ecosystem continuity, allowing users to maintain progress across devices, which serves as a defensive moat to retain users within proprietary hardware and subscription environments.

items.title: AI was supposed to destroy jobs. Where’s the carnage?
items.text: Economic data from the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research indicates that unemployment rates for workers most exposed to AI have risen by only 0.77 percentage points since 2022, trailing the 0.85 percentage-point increase seen in less-exposed sectors. The lack of mass displacement suggests that AI is currently functioning as a tool for labor augmentation rather than replacement, mirroring the slow, multi-decade integration timeline observed during the historical computer revolution.

items.title: Can AI fight AI? Where the security gap still exists in cybersecurity, and how MSPs can help.
items.text: A 2026 Proofpoint report reveals that 50% of organizations utilizing AI-based security controls still suffered from confirmed or suspicious AI-related incidents, highlighting a significant gap between rapid AI adoption and security maturity. While 87% of firms have moved AI assistants beyond pilot stages, over half lack confidence in their ability to detect compromised AI agents, creating a lucrative market opportunity for Managed Service Providers (MSPs) to bridge the operational security deficit.

items.title: Nvidia and Wall Street partners launch $500 billion AI infrastructure financing platform
items.text: Nvidia has partnered with major financial institutions including BlackRock, Blackstone, and Goldman Sachs to create a $500 billion vehicle designed to finance data centers and GPU clusters for customers. This initiative shifts AI compute from a capital-intensive purchase to a financed infrastructure asset, aiming to sustain Nvidia's revenue growth while keeping credit risk off its own balance sheet.

items.title: Meta and Nvidia expand open-weight AI model offerings to compete with proprietary systems
items.text: Nvidia released its Nemotron 3.5 Lightning model, providing developers with full access to training datasets and model weights to compete against closed-source models from OpenAI and Anthropic. The move aligns with a broader industry push to prevent premature regulatory restrictions on open-weight AI, which proponents argue will foster competition and maintain American technological leadership.

items.title: EVs dominate China’s car market: 5 takeaways from the country's latest auto sales data - CNBC
items.text: BEIJING — Survivors have emerged in China's fiercely competitive car market, which is increasingly dominated by electric-powered vehicles. Here are brands that have emerged as Chinese consumers' favorite, according...

items.text:
China’s EV sales slide again amid fading incentives, weak demand and persistent price war
A seven-month domestic downturn contrasts with a 147.8 per cent jump in overseas shipments, highlighting a widening gap...

items.title: Nvidia found a new way to keep the AI boom funded: your retirement money
items.text: Nvidia is partnering with major financial institutions like BlackRock and KKR to mobilize over $500 billion for AI infrastructure, effectively shifting the burden of capital expenditure from Big Tech balance sheets to institutional investors. By structuring AI compute as a long-term infrastructure asset similar to toll roads, these vehicles aim to securitize future cash flows from AI usage, allowing pension and insurance capital to fund the massive hardware requirements of the AI boom.

items.title: Dominion ordered to directly assign some transmission costs to data centers
items.text: The Virginia State Corporation Commission has mandated that Dominion Energy directly assign transmission infrastructure costs to data centers, moving away from broad-based rate recovery that previously impacted residential customers. This regulatory shift forces data center operators to internalize the costs of grid expansion, potentially altering the economics of site selection and increasing the capital intensity of new developments in high-demand regions.

items.title: SpaceX could make $500 billion in 2028, Elon Musk says
items.text: Elon Musk has projected that SpaceX could generate $500 billion in annual revenue by 2028, signaling an aggressive scaling of its satellite and launch operations. This valuation target implies a massive expansion beyond current launch services, likely driven by the deployment of 100,000 Starlink V3 satellites and a potential fleet of one million AI-focused data center satellites.

items.title: Firefly Aerospace pushes debut of Alpha Block 2 rocket to the fourth quarter of 2026
items.text: Firefly Aerospace reported a $25.8 million increase in R&D costs for Q2 2026, primarily attributed to production scaling for its Alpha Block 2 configuration and associated engineering upgrades. Despite the launch delay to Q4 2026, the company has secured the majority of its 2027 launch manifest and expanded its hypersonic task orders, indicating strong commercial and government demand.

items.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
items.text: Enterprise AI agents currently have access to only 45% of organizational data on average, creating a significant bottleneck for autonomous decision-making. Gartner projects that AI agents will automate or augment 50% of business decisions by 2027, necessitating a shift away from restrictive legacy data architectures. Data leaders who provide agents with access to over 70% of enterprise information report higher ROI and greater success compared to laggards who provide access to 30% or less. Effective agentic AI requires frictionless, real-time integration across structured and unstructured data sources, including supply chain and HR systems, to ensure trustworthy outcomes.

items.title: Chengdu Auto Show opens next week with nearly 120 brands, 1,600 vehicles
items.text: - The 2026 Chengdu Auto Show will cover 220,000 square meters, making it China's first A-level show of the second half of the year. - BYD will have a dedicated group pavilion in Hall 9, with Huawei's HIMA, Xpeng and Nio also attending. The 29th Chengdu International Automobile Exhibition (2026 Chengdu Auto Show) will be held from August 21 to 30 at the Western China Expo City in Chengdu, Sichuan province, making it China's first A-level auto show... The show will cover 220,000 square meters and bring together nearly 120 domestic and international brands as well as about 1,600 display vehicles, the organizer said on Wednesday. As one of China's five A-level auto shows, the Chengdu event is seen as a barometer of demand in the southwestern Chinese market.

items.title: Hyundai's first Ioniq model for China to open pre-sales at Chengdu Auto Show
items.text: - The Ioniq V is the first production model in China from Hyundai's electric brand Ioniq, and will officially launch in September. - The mid-size electric sedan was developed under the lead of Hyundai's China design center, tailored for Chinese users and planned for export to global markets. Hyundai's electric comeback in China is about to deliver its first result. Beijing Hyundai's Ioniq V will open pre-sales on August 21 at the 2026 Chengdu Auto Show and go on sale officially in September. That timeline comes from reports by several Chinese auto media, with the September launch previously disclosed by Beijing Hyundai general manager Li Fenggang.

items.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
items.text: - Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units. - The key variable for the second half is the new Sky Nomad product line. Xiaomi EV, the electric vehicle unit of Xiaomi (HKEX: 1810), delivered 31,267 vehicles in July, up 2.68% year-on-year but down 9.99% from june, according to data released Tuesday by the China Passenger Car... This marked Xiaomi EV's fourth consecutive month with deliveries above 30,000 units, although year-on-year growth was nearly flat. The company delivered 30,452 vehicles in July last year.

items.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
items.text: Synopsys has introduced the industry's first 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, designed to support linear drive optics in high-speed AI infrastructure. Transitioning to linear optics eliminates the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers, potentially reducing module power consumption by up to 50%. The new PHY IP addresses critical thermal and latency bottlenecks in dense AI racks, providing a scalable path toward 224G/448G connectivity and co-packaged optics (CPO). Measured performance data indicates that the IP meets or exceeds OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 specifications for TX VMA, jitter, and RX JTOL, ensuring interoperability in high-speed data center environments.

items.title: mikehasa/agentacct
items.text: Tech Stack: Python-based local-first architecture designed to intercept and parse agent logs. Purpose: Provides granular visibility into agentic workflows, including token consumption, latency, and tool execution success. Use Cases: Financial auditing of AI development costs, debugging agentic task failures, and optimizing prompt engineering for cost-efficiency. Compatibility: Supports popular coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenDevin. A local-first observability and cost-tracking dashboard specifically designed for AI coding agents.

items.title: simonlin1212/vibe-astock
items.text: Tech Stack: Python-based dashboard that separates deterministic financial calculations from AI-driven narrative synthesis. Purpose: Visualizes market sentiment, liquidity flow, and 'money-making' effects without relying on LLM hallucinations for core data. Use Cases: Real-time monitoring of A-share limit-up pools, ladder tiers, and institutional capital flows for short-term traders. Privacy: Operates entirely locally, allowing users to integrate LLMs for analysis without exposing sensitive trading data via API keys. A local-first A-share market sentiment and short-term trading dashboard using deterministic metrics.

items.title: Flaminis/Dalaran
items.text: Tech Stack: Rust-based architecture, hard-forked from Rerun, optimized for high-throughput robotics and sensor data. Purpose: Provides a robust framework for visualizing and analyzing complex, time-synchronized multimodal datasets. Use Cases: Analyzing high-frequency financial time-series data, sensor fusion in robotics, and debugging complex event-driven systems. Compatibility: Native support for existing .rrd recordings and seamless integration with ROS 2 ecosystems. A high-performance, ROS 2-native visualization and data infrastructure for multimodal time-series analysis.
